correctness.rationale: The 14 translates of (0,1,3) and (0,1,5) on Z/7 define an orientable 7-vertex torus with complete one-skeleton. All 99 induced subsets of cardinality 3..7 have H1 presentations in fundamental cycle coordinates with integral unit-Smith boundary matrices. Independent code reconstructs the ranks by subset size (21,49,42,14,2) and the signed inclusion differential matrices with sizes 49×21,42×49,14×42,2×14. Independently computed integer Smith ranks are (20,29,12,2) with every nonzero invariant equal to 1, and every adjacent differential product zero. Their homology therefore survives in H1 horizontal degrees ℓ=3,5 only, each Z. Empty-set H_{-1}=Z and the full torus orientation H2=Z give (0,0),(-1,6),(-3,10),(-4,14). No remaining vertical contributions; torsion-free integral universal coefficients applies. This is exhaustive for this finite complex, not inference from finite random tests.

value.rationale: The minimal seven-vertex orientable torus is a distinguished, already motivating non-spherical complex. Exact torsion-sensitive double-cohomology groups are natural invariants and a complete answer for that object, with four nonzero bigrades; a finite exact invariant need not be an infinite-family theorem to be valuable. This is a complete integral double-cohomology invariant of the seven-vertex minimal orientable torus, not a routine deduction from its ordinary homology.
